Spelthorne's population increased by around 7,400 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

The population passed 100,000

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of Spelthorne increased by 7.7%, from around 95,600 in 2011 to around 103,000 in 2021.

The population here increased at a similar rate to the overall population of the South East (7.5%), but by a greater percentage than the overall population of England (up 6.6% since the 2011 Census).

In 2021, Spelthorne was home to around 16.4 people per football pitch-sized piece of land, compared with 15.2 in 2011. This area was among the top 30% most densely populated English local authority areas at the last census.

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

Population growth was similar in Spelthorne to the South East as a whole

Median age stable in Spelthorne

The latest census data also show that the average (median) age remained 41 years in Spelthorne between the last two censuses.

This area had a similar average (median) age to the South East as a whole in 2021 (41 years) but a slightly higher average (median) age than England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 50 to 64 years rose by just over 2,900 (an increase of 16.8%), while the number of residents between 20 and 24 years fell by around 250 (5.0% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 50 and 64 years increased by 1.5 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

Family in Spelthorne

The percentage of households including a couple with dependent children increased in Spelthorne, but fell across the South East.

In Spelthorne, the percentage of households including a couple with dependent children rose from 21.4% in 2011 to 21.8% in 2021. During the same period, the regional percentage fell from 21.0% to 20.6%.

The percentage of households including a couple without children in Spelthorne fell from 16.8% to 15.5%, while the percentage of households including a couple with only non-dependent children remained at 7.5%.

The percentage of households including a couple with dependent children in Spelthorne increased by 0.4 percentage points

Spelthorne residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 79,300 Spelthorne residents said they were born in England. This represented 77.1% of the local population. The figure has decreased from just over 79,400 in 2011, which at the time represented 83.1% of Spelthorne's population.

India was the next most represented, with just over 3,900 Spelthorne residents reporting this country of birth (3.8%). This figure was up from just under 2,200 in 2011, which at the time represented 2.3% of the population of Spelthorne.

The number of Spelthorne residents born in Poland rose from around 950 in 2011 (1.0% of the local population) to around 2,000 in 2021 (1.9%).

In 2021, 77.1% of Spelthorne residents reported their country of birth as England

Fall in home ownership

Spelthorne saw the South East's largest percentage-point fall in the proportion of households that owned their home (from 72.6% in 2011 to 68.1% in 2021).

Reading saw the South East's next largest decrease in the percentage of households that owned their home (from 54.8% in 2011 to 50.4% in 2021).

Across the South East, the percentage of households that owned their home fell from 67.6% to 65.7%, while the percentage in nearby Runnymede fell from 69.5% to 66.4%.

The rate of home ownership in Spelthorne decreased by 4.5 percentage points

Ethnic groups in Spelthorne

In 2021, 12.8% of Spelthorne residents identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category, up from 7.6% in 2011. The 5.1 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across the South East, the percentage of people from the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" ethnic group increased from 5.2% to 7.0%, while across England the percentage increased from 7.8% to 9.6%.

In 2021, 78.7% of people in Spelthorne identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 87.3% in 2011), while 3.7% identified their ethnic group within the "Mixed or Multiple" category (compared with 2.5% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Black, Black British, Black Welsh, Caribbean or African" category increased from 1.6% in 2011 to 2.5% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.

In 2021, 12.8% of usual residents in Spelthorne identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category

National identity in Spelthorne

The percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK increased in Spelthorne, while the percentage remained stable in nearby Runnymede.

In Spelthorne, the percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity increased from 8.1% in 2011 to 10.9% in 2021. During the same period, the percentage in nearby Runnymede remained 11.4%.

The percentage of people who identified with a UK and non-UK national identity in Spelthorne increased from 1.1% to 2.5%, while the percentage of people who identified as "British only" increased from 17.5% to 54.7%.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in Spelthorne increased by 2.8 percentage points

Unpaid care in Spelthorne

In 2021, 4.6% of Spelthorne residents (aged five years and over) reported providing up to 19 hours of unpaid care each week. This figure decreased from 7.5% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, 1.6% of residents (aged five years and over) reported providing between 20 and 49 hours of unpaid care each week, compared with 1.3% in 2011. The proportion of Spelthorne residents (aged five years and over) that provided at least 50 hours of weekly unpaid care increased from 2.3% to 2.4%.

The decrease in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Spelthorne (2.9 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the South East (2.8 percentage points, from 7.3% to 4.5%). Across England, the proportion fell by 2.8 percentage points, from 7.2% to 4.4%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Spelthorne decreased by 2.9 percentage points

Religion in Spelthorne

In 2021, 31.2% of Spelthorne residents reported having "No religion", up from 22.5% in 2011. The rise of 8.7 percentage points was the largest increase of all broad religious groups in Spelthorne. Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across the South East, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 27.7% to 40.2%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 50.9% of people in Spelthorne described themselves as Christian (down from 63.8%), while 5.7% did not state their religion (down from 7.0% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

Read the bulletin Religion, England and Wales: Census 2021.

In 2021, 31.2% of usual residents in Spelthorne reported having "No religion"

Unemployment in Spelthorne

In 2021, 3.1% of Spelthorne residents (aged 16 years and over) said they were unemployed. This figure was at a similar level in 2011 (2.9%).

Spelthorne saw England's joint third-largest rise (alongside Richmond upon Thames) in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were unemployed.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were unemployed (excluding full-time students) in Spelthorne increased by 0.2 percentage points

Change in work hours

In 2021, 9.7% of Spelthorne residents aged 16 years and over and in employment said they worked 15 hours or less per week. This figure increased from 8.7% in 2011.

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked 15 hours or less per week was greater in Spelthorne (1.0 percentage points) than across the South East (0.5 percentage points, from 10.4% to 11.0%). Across England, the percentage increased by 0.6 percentage points, from 9.7% to 10.3%.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The percentage of adults who worked 15 hours or less in Spelthorne increased by 1.0 percentage points

Health in Spelthorne

In 2021, 49.8% of Spelthorne residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 47.0% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" fell from 36.1% to 34.8%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of Spelthorne residents describing their health as "very bad" remained 0.9%, while those describing their health as "bad" fell from 3.4% to 3.0%.

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

In 2021, 0.9% of usual residents said their health was very bad in Spelthorne

More adults never married or in a civil partnership

Of Spelthorne residents aged 16 years and over, 34.2% said they had never been married or in a civil partnership in 2021, up from 31.5% in 2011.

The increase in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had never been married or in a civil partnership in Spelthorne (2.8 percentage points) was similar to the increase across the South East (2.9 percentage points, from 31.9% to 34.8%). Across England, the percentage increased by 3.3 percentage points, from 34.6% to 37.9%.

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who had never married or registered a civil partnership in Spelthorne increased by 2.8 percentage points

Disability in Spelthorne

In 2021, 5.7% of Spelthorne residents were identified as being disabled and limited a lot. This figure decreased from 6.8% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, just under 1 in 11 people (8.7%) were identified as being disabled and limited a little, compared with 8.9% in 2011. The proportion of Spelthorne residents who were not disabled increased from 84.3% to 85.6%.

The decrease in the proportion of residents who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Spelthorne (1.1 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the South East (1.0 percentage points, from 7.2% to 6.2%). Across England, the proportion fell by 1.6 percentage points, from 9.1% to 7.5%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Spelthorne decreased by 1.1 percentage points
